readers.reasoning: The linear clause with the ref modifier on declare simd for dummy x is legal. OpenMP 5.2 requires that with ref the list items be polymorphic, assumed-shape, or allocatable. x is an assumed-shape dummy without VALUE, so it satisfies the rule; the reported diagnostic states the restriction inverted. The program has no race. A conforming compiler must accept it.

The Fortran restriction for linear on declare simd says that with the ref modifier the list items must be polymorphic variables, assumed-shape arrays, or allocatables. x is an assumed-shape dummy without VALUE, so linear(x: ref) is required, not forbidden; the compiler's message states the opposite. Nothing else in the program breaks a rule: the SIMD directive may be ignored, the call is sequential on the device, and a(i:i) is a valid actual argument. A conforming compiler must accept it.
